title: Does the lamp turn on?
instruction: The program of a night lamp on a micro:bit. Step through it for each situation.
debrief: With “and” the lamp turns on only when both conditions hold. With “or” one is enough. And the decision has to run in a loop, otherwise it wouldn't react to changes.

code: if it is dark and the sensor detects movement:

steps.input: Dark, someone is walking around the room
steps.why: Both parts hold: it is dark and the sensor detected movement.
There is no movement. With “and” both parts must hold.
It isn't dark, so the first part doesn't hold.

steps.input: Dark, a cat ran past the sensor
steps.why: A motion sensor can't tell a cat from a person. For the program it is movement.

steps.q: Why is the whole decision inside “forever”?
options: so that it decides only once after switching on
so that the lamp reacts even if the situation changes a minute later
because you can't write a condition without a loop
steps.why: Without a loop the program would decide once after switching on. It wouldn't react to darkness or movement later.

rounds.title: Someone changed “and” to “or”
code: if it is dark or the sensor detects movement:

steps.input: Noon, the sun is shining, someone walked past
steps.why: With “or” one part is enough. Movement is enough, so the lamp is on even at noon and drains the battery.
